A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe CM4IR. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments, PSNR/LPIPS comparisons, runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative results on LSUN Bedroom and Cat.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds ImageNet results and a hyperparameter sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same initialization, back-projection guidance, denoising/noise-injection decoupling, and sign-reversed estimated noise. Revised task-specific hyperparameters do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds ImageNet 64×64 evaluation with bicubic 2× super-resolution at noise levels 0.01, 0.025, and 0.05. This extends coverage beyond the retained LSUN Bedroom/Cat 256×256 experiments to another dataset and a distinct low-resolution restoration scenario.

E2.justification: DPS joins the qualitative comparisons in Figures 1–2; v1 already evaluated DPS quantitatively for super-resolution in Appendix B.4. The relocated Bedroom example also gains CM(40) and CoSIGN panels in v2 Figure 9. Existing quantitative comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 5 revises deblurring noise schedules and some regularization parameters, sets Bedroom deblurring δ values to zero, and changes the Bedroom super-resolution δ sequence at noise 0.05. Figure 8 introduces controlled sweeps of η and paired scheduling parameters. Existing LSUN sample counts, metrics, and principal NFE budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2/Figure 8 tests sensitivity to η and paired initial-noise/decay settings for Bedroom super-resolution at noise 0.025. Conversely, Table 6 removes both Bedroom deblurring rows comparing δ=0 against δ>0. Other component ablations and NFE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sensitivity curves show performance across parameter settings without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds ImageNet comparisons showing CM4IR has the highest PSNR but worse LPIPS than DDRM at all three noise levels; Figure 8 adds sensitivity results. Tables 2–3 replace four deblurring score pairs alongside revised settings: for example, Bedroom at noise 0.025 changes from 28.85/0.217 to 29.00/0.213 PSNR/LPIPS. Table 6 removes deblurring ablation results, and several qualitative outputs are added or updated.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Proposition 3.1, its Appendix A induction proof, and the connection to Polyak acceleration remain substantively identical.

C1.justification: The central claims remain four-NFE zero-shot restoration, the proposed noise-injection mechanism, and its usefulness for accelerating guided diffusion methods. The conclusion drops its closing CoSIGN discussion, but that limitation remains stated elsewhere in the paper.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly interprets stability under moderate parameter changes and explains pairing initial-noise and decay parameters. Appendix B.8 explains choosing 2× super-resolution for low-resolution ImageNet images. Existing interpretations of CoSIGN's mismatch limitations and few-step diffusion performance remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly identifies the Google Hugging Face location used for pretrained diffusion models, and Table 5 revises exact hyperparameter recipes. The CM4IR repository link already appeared in v1 Appendix B; repeating it in v2's abstract does not establish a new code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tirer et al., 'Deep internal learning: Deep learning from a single input,' to the discussion of task-specific models under mismatch. It also clarifies the role of an existing reference on back-projection convergence rates. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise limited prose additions, a shortened conclusion, updated acknowledgments, and two new appendix subsections with subsequent renumbering. The main narrative, section organization, and method exposition remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 gain DPS panels and zoomed details, with a different example in Figure 2. v2 adds sensitivity Figure 8 and ImageNet Table 11, expands and regroups appendix illustrations, and corrects several table captions. Most existing displays retain their design and content.

improvement.justification: ImageNet comparisons and direct parameter-sensitivity evidence modestly strengthen validation, while model-source information and zoomed illustrations improve usability. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of deblurring ablation evidence. The gains remain bounded: ImageNet-specific sampling and tuning details are unclear, and revised deblurring scores accompany changed settings rather than establishing same-setting improvements.
